chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Ya'qub from Abu Basir said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I pray, then I enter the mosque and the prayer is established, although I have already prayed.' He said: 'Pray with them, for Allah will choose the one He loves more of the two.'

key_terms.تُقَامُ الصَّلَاةُ: The prayer is established (congregational prayer begins)

ai.seo_question: What should I do if I have already prayed but enter the mosque while the congregation is praying?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs a companion who had already prayed individually to join the congregational prayer, highlighting the virtue of *fada'il al-jama'ah* (merits of congregation) even for those who have fulfilled their obligation. The phrase 'Allah chooses the one more beloved to Him' is interpreted by Shia scholars as indicating that the reward is not merely mechanical but reflects divine preference for the act of communal worship and humility. This ruling underscores the social and spiritual significance of the mosque as a center for unity, encouraging believers to maintain their connection to the community even after personal devotion.
